rationale: Sixth investigation: the consequence of the two-leader overlap, which the previous obligation left as its remaining question. The obligation c-committed-entry-stored-by-quorum states that an entry a node reports as committed at an index must be the entry a quorum of the voting configuration stores there, because the commit rule assumes that entries with the same index and term are identical. The check builds the overlap with the harness of the previous finding, keeps the two leaders from reaching each other, and then lets one of them commit a client write: the leader acknowledges the command at an index where the other voter already holds a different entry with the same index and term, so the acknowledgement rests on a quorum that does not hold the command. No map change is needed: the obligation is registered on the existing commit-index fact through the commitment behavior that establishes it and the client contract behavior that consumes it.

candidate.rationale: Sixth Candidate, opened from the question the two-leader obligation recorded as remaining. It states what a committed index must mean for the client and binds it to the commitment rule that decides it.

question.question: Can a leader acknowledge a client write at a log index where the other voters of the configuration store a different entry, i.e. can a reported commit index name an entry that the configuration does not hold?
question.importance: A client write that is acknowledged must be the entry the configuration stored: the whole purpose of committing by quorum is that the acknowledged value survives and that every replica applies the same commands in the same order. If a leader can count a quorum for a command the other voter never applied, the acknowledgement is false - the client acts on a value that no other replica holds - and the log positions of the two leaders diverge with the same index and term, so any later read, leader change or recovery can surface a different history for the same committed position. The enabling chain (two leaders of one term, one of which proposed a term it had already voted in after its published term dropped) was confirmed separately, so the remaining question is what the acknowledgement actually guarantees.
participants: the two leaders of one term
the client whose write is acknowledged
objects: the log entry at one index on two voters
the FSM applied values of both voters
contexts: three voters with two leaders of the same term that cannot reach each other but both reach the third
a client write issued to one of the two leaders
event_paths: leader path: Apply appends the command at the next index, replicates it to the reachable voter and commits when the tracked match index reaches a majority
voter path: the reachable voter already holds an entry at that index with the same term, so the conflict loop treats the incoming entry as a duplicate and replies success without storing it
observation: the leader's log and applied value at the acknowledged index are compared with the voter's log entry and applied value at the same index

supporting_behavior_ids.b-follower-append-entries: the conflict handling that skips a same-index same-term entry is what turns the voter's acknowledgement into a false match
supporting_behavior_ids.b-elect-self: the path that produced the second leader of the term, which is the enabling condition of the whole chain

counterevidence: Under a single leadership the assumption that equal index and term imply an equal entry is sound, so the conflict handling is correct wherever one leader exists per term.
The voter's acknowledgement is honest about its own log position: it did store an entry there, just not the one the leader sent.
The chain needs two leaders of one term, which was confirmed as reachable but is itself transient unless the two are kept apart, so the observation depends on that fault.
Nothing here shows a second client read of the wrong value; the divergence is at the log and applied values of one index.
unknowns: how long the divergent positions survive once the two leaders can exchange traffic again
whether a client read routed to the other leader returns the other command
whether recovery or a snapshot of either leader exposes the divergence differently
question.trigger_rationale: A follower that already holds an entry at the same index compares only terms: when the terms match it treats the incoming entry as a duplicate and stores nothing, then reports success, so the leader records the voter's match at that index and its commitment reaches a majority. With two leaders of one term writing different entries at the same index, that reply tells the leader the position is written without asserting that the same command is written there, and the client's future completes without error.

obligation.description: An entry that a node reports as committed at index I must be the entry that a quorum of the voting configuration stores at I, so a client write may not be acknowledged at a position where the other voters hold a different entry. The requirement binds the commit rule and the acknowledgement path together, because committing by quorum assumes that entries with the same index and term are identical.

scope.description: A cluster of voters in the captured module, with a client write issued to a leader while another leader holds the same term and both can reach a common voter.
assumptions: the client treats a successful Apply future as an acknowledgement that the value is the one the configuration holds
the common voter is reachable from both leaders

the durability of the acknowledged entry after a later recovery, which this check does not exercise
behaviour of clients or transports outside the module

grounding.derivation: Commitment advances the leader's commit index to the majority position among the tracked voter matches, and each match is the position a voter acknowledged in that leader's log (s-commitment-recalc, s-raft-append-commit). The follower's conflict handling compares terms only and skips an entry whose index and term it already holds, replying success (s-raft-append-entries-log), and a configuration change is written as an ordinary entry of the log (s-raft-append-config). When two leaders of one term hold different entries at the same index - reachable because the candidate path can propose a term already voted in and the vote path still grants it - the acknowledgement a client receives names a position the configuration does not store that command at.
grounding.applicability: Applies when two nodes hold the leadership of one term and can each reach a common voter; the check stages that overlap in a three-voter cluster.
unresolved: whether the divergence survives the next leader change
whether a client read can observe it
alternatives: the follower could compare entry contents as well as terms, which the captured implementation does not do
the two leaders could be allowed to exchange traffic, which ends the overlap before any write

associations.rationale: This entry point is the located implementation of the requirement: it turns the tracked voter positions into the commit index a client relies on, and the positions it counts come from acknowledgements that compare terms but not entry contents.

bindings.description: commitment.recalculate advances the leader's commit index to the majority of the tracked voter match indexes, so the value a client is told is committed is exactly this rule's output.
